name: Junkyard Dog
manufacturer: None — kitbash builds from scrapyard parts
description: Not a model. A category. The generic term for any ground vehicle assembled from scrap — welded-together car frames, mismatched wheels, engines pulled from industrial equipment, steering columns from boats. Every Junker is unique because every Junker is built from whatever was available. They belch smoke, they rattle, they break down constantly, and they are the only cars most Tier 1 residents will ever own. Some are works of desperate art.
propulsion: Varies wildly — electric, hydrogen, biodiesel, compressed air, stolen fuel cells, or unknowable combinations
speed: 20-60 km/h depending on build quality and prayer
capacity: 2-6, depending on how many seats were welded in
range: Varies. 'Until it stops' is the honest answer.
cost: Φ100-500 depending on quality and desperation
autonomy: Manual only. Many lack basic safety features.
armament: Whatever the builder bolted on. Ramming plates are common.
common_usage: Families who need to move heavy loads, mechanics who built them as a point of pride, anyone who found enough parts to make something that moves.
story_hooks: A Junker builder discovers a military-grade power cell in a scrapyard that makes their vehicle terrifyingly fast
The Junker racing circuit in the industrial district is a front for a much larger underground economy
physical_description: A patchwork chassis of welded steel frames, mismatched fenders, and cannibalized engine blocks—no two Junkers look alike. Rust blooms across primer-gray panels; vinyl seats are duct-taped and split; the windshield is often cracked or replaced with salvaged acrylic. Smoke leaks from seams and exhaust ports; the frame rattles with every pothole, held together by hope, wire, and spot welds that glow cherry-red in the rain.
